kNEHotspotHelperResultCommandNotRecogniz.doc: The helper did not recognize the command type.

kNEHotspotHelperResultFailure.doc: The command failed to be handled.

NEOnDemandRuleActionDisconnect.doc: Do not start the VPN connection, and disconnect the VPN connection if it is not currently disconnected.

NEOnDemandRuleActionEvaluateConnection.doc: Start the VPN after evaluating the destination host being accessed against the rule’s parameters.

NEOnDemandRuleActionIgnore.doc: Do not start the VPN connection, but do not disconnect it if it is currently connected.

NEProviderStopReasonNoNetworkAvailable.doc: No network connectivity is currently available.

NEProviderStopReasonProviderFailed.doc: The provider failed to function correctly.

NEProviderStopReasonSuperceded.doc: The configuration was superceded by a higher-priority configuration.

NEVPNConnectionError.doc: Error codes specific to VPN connections.

NEVPNConnectionErrorAuthenticationFailed.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the VPN server rejected the user credentials.

NEVPNConnectionErrorClientCertificateExp.doc: An error code that indicates the client certfiicate’s validity period has passed.

NEVPNConnectionErrorClientCertificateInv.doc: An error code that indicates the client certfiicate is invalid.

NEVPNConnectionErrorClientCertificateNot.doc: An error code that indicates the client certfiicate won’t be valid until some time in the future.

NEVPNConnectionErrorConfigurationFailed.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the configuration is invalid.

NEVPNConnectionErrorConfigurationNotFoun.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the system couldn’t find a configuration.

NEVPNConnectionErrorNegotiationFailed.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the negotiation failed.

NEVPNConnectionErrorNoNetworkAvailable.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the system isn’t connected to a network.

NEVPNConnectionErrorOverslept.doc: An error code that indicates the system slept for an extended period of time, causing the VPN connection to terminate.

NEVPNConnectionErrorPluginDisabled.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN plugin isn’t available or needs an update.

NEVPNConnectionErrorPluginFailed.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN plugin failed unexpectedly.

NEVPNConnectionErrorServerAddressResolut.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the system couldn’t determine the VPN server address.

NEVPNConnectionErrorServerCertificateExp.doc: An error code that indicates the server certfiicate’s validity period has passed.

NEVPNConnectionErrorServerCertificateInv.doc: An error code that indicates the server certfiicate is invalid.

NEVPNConnectionErrorServerCertificateNot.doc: An error code that indicates the server certfiicate won’t be valid until some time in the future.

NEVPNConnectionErrorServerDead.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the VPN server has stopped responding.

NEVPNConnectionErrorServerDisconnected.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the VPN server terminated the connection.

NEVPNConnectionErrorServerNotResponding.doc: An error code that indicates the VPN connection failed because the VPN server isn’t responding.

NEVPNConnectionErrorUnrecoverableNetwork.doc: An error code that indicates network conditions changed such that the VPN connection needed to terminate.

NEVPNError.doc: Information about an error encountered while configuring or using a VPN.

NEVPNIKEAuthenticationMethod.doc: Internet Key Exchange (IKE) authentication methods used to authenticate with the IPSec server.

NEVPNIKEAuthenticationMethodCertificate.doc: Use a certificate and private key as the authentication credential. The certificate and private key set in the identityReference or identityData property will be used.

NEVPNIKEAuthenticationMethodNone.doc: Do not authenticate with the IPSec server. Note that extended authentication may still be performed if the useExtendedAuthentication property is set. This value is only valid for IKE version 2 (IKEv2)

NEVPNIKEAuthenticationMethodSharedSecret.doc: Use a shared secret as the authentication credential. The shared secret set in the sharedSecretReference property will be used.

NEVPNIKEv2CertificateType.doc: An enumeration of certificate type values.

NEVPNIKEv2CertificateTypeECDSA256.doc: The ECDSA with p-256 curve certificate type.

NEVPNIKEv2CertificateTypeECDSA384.doc: The ECDSA with p-384 curve certificate type.

NEVPNIKEv2CertificateTypeECDSA521.doc: The ECDSA with p-521 curve certificate type.

NEVPNIKEv2DeadPeerDetectionRate.doc: An enumeration of values for the frequency at which the IKEv2 client runs the dead peer detection algorithm.

NEVPNIKEv2DeadPeerDetectionRateHigh.doc: Run dead peer detection once every 1 minute. If the peer does not respond, retry 5 times at 1 second intervals before declaring the peer dead and terminating the session.

NEVPNIKEv2DeadPeerDetectionRateLow.doc: Run dead peer detection once every 30 minutes. If the peer does not respond, retry 5 times at 1 second intervals before declaring the peer dead and terminating the session.

NEVPNIKEv2DeadPeerDetectionRateMedium.doc: Run dead peer detection once every 10 minutes. If the peer does not respond, retry 5 times at 1 second intervals before declaring the peer dead and terminating the session.

NEVPNIKEv2DeadPeerDetectionRateNone.doc: Do not perform dead peer detection.

NEVPNIKEv2DiffieHellmanGroup.doc: An enumeration of Diffie-Hellman group values.

NEVPNIKEv2DiffieHellmanGroup19.doc: Diffie Hellman group 19 (256-bit random elliptic curve group over GF[P] [ECP]).

NEVPNIKEv2DiffieHellmanGroup20.doc: Diffie Hellman group 20 (384-bit random elliptic curve group over GF[P] [ECP]).

NEVPNIKEv2DiffieHellmanGroup21.doc: Diffie Hellman group 21 (521-bit random elliptic curve group over GF[P] [ECP]).

NEVPNIKEv2DiffieHellmanGroupInvalid.doc: A value indicating the group is not a valid Diffie-Hellman group.

NEVPNIKEv2EncryptionAlgorithm.doc: An enumeration of encryption algorithm values.

NEVPNIKEv2PostQuantumKeyExchangeMethod.doc: Quantum-secure key exchange methods you use with IKEv2 servers.

NEVPNIKEv2PostQuantumKeyExchangeMethod36.doc: Instructs the server to use the ML-KEM-768 key exchange method.

NEVPNIKEv2PostQuantumKeyExchangeMethod37.doc: Instructs the server to use the ML-KEM-1024 key exchange method.

NEVPNIKEv2PostQuantumKeyExchangeMethodNo.doc: Instructs the server not to use a quantum-secure key exchange method.

NEVPNIKEv2TLSVersion.doc: An enumeration of TLS Versions for use in EAP-TLS.

NEVPNIKEv2TLSVersion1_0.doc: A value to use TLS version 1.0.

NEVPNIKEv2TLSVersion1_1.doc: A value to use TLS version 1.1.

NEVPNIKEv2TLSVersion1_2.doc: A value to use TLS version 1.2.

NEVPNIKEv2TLSVersionDefault.doc: A value to use the default TLS configuration.

NEVPNStatus.doc: The possible states of a VPN connection.

NEVPNStatusConnecting.doc: The VPN is in the process of connecting.

NEVPNStatusDisconnecting.doc: The VPN is in the process of disconnecting.

NEVPNStatusInvalid.doc: The associated VPN configuration doesn’t exist in the Network Extension preferences or isn’t enabled.

NEVPNStatusReasserting.doc: The VPN is in the process of reconnecting.

NWPathStatusSatisfiable.doc: The path is not currently satisfied, but may become satisfied upon a connection attempt. This can be due to a service, such as a VPN or a cellular data connection not being activated.

NWPathStatusSatisfied.doc: The path is ready to be used for network connections.

NWPathStatusUnsatisfied.doc: The path for network connections is not available, either due to lack of network connectivity or being prohibited by system policy.

NWTCPConnectionState.doc: Defined connection states. New types may be defined in the future.

NWTCPConnectionStateCancelled.doc: The connection has been cancelled by the client calling cancel.

NWTCPConnectionStateConnected.doc: The connection is established. It is now possible to transfer data. If TLS is in use, the TLS handshake has finished.

NWTCPConnectionStateConnecting.doc: The connection is attempting to connect. This includes endpoint resolution when applicable.

NWTCPConnectionStateDisconnected.doc: The connection is disconnected. It is no longer possible to transfer data. The application should call cancel to clean up resources.

NWTCPConnectionStateInvalid.doc: The connection is in an invalid or uninitialized state.

NWTCPConnectionStateWaiting.doc: The connection has attempted to connect but failed. It is now waiting for better conditions before trying again.

NWUDPSessionStateCancelled.doc: The session has been cancelled by the client calling cancel.

NWUDPSessionStateFailed.doc: None of the currently resolved endpoints can be used at this time, either due to problems with the path or the client rejecting the endpoints.

NWUDPSessionStateInvalid.doc: The session is in an invalid or uninitialized state.

NWUDPSessionStatePreparing.doc: The remote endpoint is being resolved.

NWUDPSessionStateReady.doc: The session is ready for reading and writing data.

NWUDPSessionStateWaiting.doc: The session is waiting for better conditions before attempting to make the session ready.

serverCertificateCommonName.doc: A string containing the value of the Subject Common Name field of the IKEv2 server’s certificate.

serverCertificateIssuerCommonName.doc: A string containing the value of the Subject Common Name field of the Certificate Authority certificate that issued the IKEv2 server’s certificate.

strictRevocationCheck.doc: Require a “not revoked” result when checking if the certificate identifying the server is revoked.

useConfigurationAttributeInternalIPSubne.doc: A Boolean indicating whether or not the IKEv2 client should use the INTERNAL_IP4_SUBNET and/or INTERNAL_IP6_SUBNET attributes sent by the IKEv2 server.

authenticationMethod.doc: The method used to authenticate the device with the IPSec server. For IKE version 2, when using extended authentication, this authentication method only affects how the client validates the authentication payload presented by the server.

localIdentifier.doc: A string identifying the iOS or macOS device for authentication purposes

remoteIdentifier.doc: A string identifying the IPSec server for authentication purposes

sharedSecretReference.doc: A persistent keychain reference to a keychain item containing the IKE shared secret.

useExtendedAuthentication.doc: A flag indicating if extended authentication will be negotiated.

domain.doc: The endpoint’s Bonjour service domain, such as "local".

port.doc: The endpoint’s port, represented as a string.

constrained.doc: A Boolean that indicates whether or not the path uses a constrained interface, such as when using low-data mode.

expensive.doc: A Boolean that indicates whether or not the path uses an expensive interface.

status.doc: The evaluated status of the network path.

connectedPath.doc: The network path over which the connection was established.

endpoint.doc: The destination endpoint with which this connection was created.

hasBetterPath.doc: If a connection has a better path, new connections would use a different interface.

localAddress.doc: The IP address endpoint from which the connection was established.

remoteAddress.doc: The IP address endpoint to which the connection was established.

txtRecord.doc: The TXT record associated with a connected Bonjour service endpoint.

viable.doc: The viability of a TCP connection indicates whether or not data can be transferred.

SSLCipherSuites.doc: The set of allowed cipher suites when negotiating TLS.

TLSSessionID.doc: The Session ID to use for the associated TCP connection.

maximumSSLProtocolVersion.doc: The maximum allowed SSLProtocol value to use when negotiating TLS.

minimumSSLProtocolVersion.doc: The minimum allowed SSLProtocol value to use when negotiating TLS.

currentPath.doc: The current evaluated path for the session’s resolvedEndpoint property.

endpoint.doc: The destination endpoint with which this session was created.

hasBetterPath.doc: If a session has a better path, new session would use a different interface.

maximumDatagramLength.doc: The maximum size of a datagram to be written currently.

state.doc: The current state of the UDP session.

viable.doc: The viability of a UDP session represents whether or not data can be transferred.
